surprises.body: Boston usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 58 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 108 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Three power-play goals get DiPietro his first NHL win
paras: Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored 21 seconds apart late in the first to put the Ducks up 2-0, but they didn’t score again. Frédéric Brunet, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by James Hagens, on the power play early in the second to get the Bruins on the board. David Pastrňák and Elias Lindholm scored power-play goals just under five minutes apart early in the third to put the Bruins ahead for good and complete the comeback. Matthew Poitras made it 4-2 with less than four minutes left, and that was that.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Michael DiPietro finally got his first NHL win, making 26 saves in his fourth start, eight seasons after his NHL debut. Lukáš Dostál stopped 18 of 22 for the Ducks.

The power plays decided it: Brunet, Pastrňák and Elias Lindholm all scored on the power play as the Bruins turned a two-goal hole into the lead, and the Ducks went 0-for-5 on theirs. Nikita Zadorov took three penalties on his own. The Bruins moved to 6-2-0, and the Ducks dropped to 4-3-0.

items.text: David Pastrňák passed Brad Marchand for fourth on the Bruins’ all-time goals list, with 423.
Four straight wins for the Bruins.
David Pastrňák extended his point streak against Anaheim to six games.
Leo Carlsson had a point in all five of his games against Boston since 2023-24, and that run ended.
